label: sec:large-scale-intro
html:
At macroscopic and cosmological scales, the same graded-trace residue that generates Strutinsky shell corrections in finite nuclei governs long-wavelength curvature defects on the substrate. This section evaluates three large-scale observational consequences of the categorical geometry:

  1. Cosmic microwave background (CMB) torsion: Non-uniformity of the q-torsion connection across the genus-4 base curve induces low-multipole angular power anomalies in the CMB temperature spectrum.
  2. Emergent gravitational coupling: Newton's gravitational constant G emerges as the universal residue prefactor of the unified mass formula.
  3. Topological defects and fluid intermittency: Cosmic-string and hopfion defect signatures in galaxy-cluster surveys connect to the high-vorticity intermittency scaling of the three-dimensional Navier–Stokes equations.
